bola_idor_enumeration.scope: Sequential or guessed object identifiers used to reach resources that belong to other subjects.
exclusions: Sequential IDs alone with no authorization context
Writing unauthorized properties of the caller's own object belongs to bopla_mass_assignment
Calling functions above the caller's role belongs to bfla_admin_function_probing
required_evidence: Trusted subject identity and resource ownership context
Request sequence with differing object IDs under one subject

bopla_mass_assignment.scope: Object-property authorization abuse: a create or update request sets properties the caller may not write (role, owner, price, balance, verification flags) through mass assignment.
exclusions: Access to another subject's whole object by identifier belongs to bola_idor_enumeration
Calling an endpoint reserved for a higher role belongs to bfla_admin_function_probing
Writes to fields the object schema marks writable for the caller's role
required_evidence: Request body with the submitted property set
Object schema or allow-list of properties writable by the caller's role
Caller role or subject context from the gateway

bfla_admin_function_probing.scope: Function-level authorization abuse: a caller with a lower role invokes or probes administrative or privileged functions (admin routes, management methods, internal operations).
exclusions: Same-role access to another subject's object belongs to bola_idor_enumeration
Privileged properties smuggled into an allowed write belong to bopla_mass_assignment
Admin routes called by a caller whose role permits them
required_evidence: Caller role from the gateway or token claims
Role the route or method requires, from trusted route configuration
Request sequence or method change showing the privileged function attempt

separating_rule: bola: the caller acts on ANOTHER subject's object id on an ordinary route with ordinary fields (ownership mismatch in authz context). bopla: the caller's OWN object on an ordinary route, but the body sets properties the object schema marks read-only for the caller's role. bfla: the route or method ITSELF requires a higher role than the caller holds; object and fields are unremarkable.
